V:
Tapodā：A large lake below the Vebhāra mountain，outside Rājagaha．The lake was cool，but the stream flowing from it，also called Tapodā （Vin．iii．108； iv．116f； DA．i．35； UdA．110），was hot．Around it was the Tapodārāma．

It is said （SA．i．30f； Sp．ii．512） that the water of the river was hot because it flowed between two Lohakumbhi-nirayas，which existed under Rājagaha．The lake was the playground of the Nāgas who dwelt at the foot of the Vebhāra mountain．Monks and recluses were evidently in the habit of going to the Tapodā to bathe in the hot springs．

Thus，we find Samiddhi being questioned by a deity as he dried himself after bathing in the Tapodā （S．i．8ff； M．iii．192ff； J．ii．56），and the Anguttara Nikāya （v．196f） records a discussion between Ananda and the paribbājaka Kokanuda，on the banks of the Tapodā，where they had gone to bathe．

pn:
Tapodārāma. A grove near lake Tapodā (q.v.). In the grove was a monastery where the Buddha seems to have stayed on several occasions. It is said that on one such occasion the Buddha gave Ānanda the chance of asking him to live for a whole kappa, but Ānanda failed to make use of it (DN.ii.116).

Near the Tapodārāma was the Tapodakandarā. They were both far from Rājagaha, and monks would come from afar late at night and, in order to test Dabba Mallaputta’s powers, ask him to provide lodgings for them (Vin.ii.76; iii.159).

tapojigucchā.p: [Tapa+jigucchā] (thī) CL=7 (1) It disgust diligence for doing unwholesome deeds. See also - Tapojigucchāhetu. (2) It establishes and disgusts unwholesome deeds which is practiced by Acelaka practice. (Acelaka means naked ascetic; lit. unclothed). (3) Diligence which can worry and disgust defilement. See also - Tapojigucchāvāda.

tapojigucchāvāda.p: [Tapojigucchā+vāda] (pu) CL=7 (1) The 'doctrine' which disgusts on diligence of unwholesome deeds. (Ti) (2) (A) One who preaches the doctrine or practice  which disgusts on diligence of unwholesome deeds. (B) One who preaches about diligence which disgusts and worries  for defilement (that is related to Vipassanā, magga, phala).

tapovana.p: [Tapa+vana] (na) CL=7 [Dhāna. 928.] It should cling and dwell by moral or upright persons (Hermits, Bhikkhus), (A) Forest, Monastery situated far from lay habitat, Monastery. (B) (Dibbavihāra) rūpāvacara jhāna. (C) 'tapovana' Monastery which situated near Anurādha City in  Sīhaḷa Island. (Dibbavihāra means supreme condition of heart) (Rūpāvacara means related to the realm of form).
pn: Tapovana. A group of monasteries near Anurādhapura inhabited by the Paṁsukūlikas. They lay in the forest district to the west of the city. Cv.lii.22; liii.14ff; also Cv.Trs.i.163, n.8.
